summary.text: 零 is a sound-and-meaning compound: 雨 supplies the rain category, while 令 is traditionally given as the sound element. The graph is used for falling rain and, in modern Chinese, zero; the path between those meanings is not fully dated here. [ref002, ref003, ref012, ref016]

formation.text: Phonosemantic. 雨 contributes the rain meaning, while 令 is the traditional phonetic analysis. A Shuowen edition instead reads the phonetic element as 霝, and the evidence does not resolve this difference. [ref003, ref012, ref019]

components.text: 雨 is the semantic component, contributing the category of rain. The received seal-script rendering shows it above 令, but no verified early inscription form establishes the graph’s earliest shape. [ref003, ref012, ref025]

令 is the traditional sound component in the Shuowen analysis. Baxter–Sagart gives one reading matching 零, but 令 has multiple readings; this supports, without uniquely establishing, the intended sound relation. [ref003, ref014, ref022]

sound_limitation.text: The matching reconstruction is reported for one 令 reading, and the evidence does not identify it uniquely as the reading intended in this graph. [ref014, ref022]

sound.text: One 令 reading and 零 are both reconstructed as Old Chinese *[r]ˤiŋ and given Middle Chinese leng in the Baxter–Sagart system. The same modern Mandarin líng is reported for 零 and this 令 entry, but 令 has other readings. [ref014, ref022]
sound.system: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction; Middle Chinese source notation; Mandarin as reported in the same table

history.text: The selected seal-script image is a modern digital redraw of a form transmitted in the Shuowen tradition, not an ancient artifact image. It depicts 雨 above 令; it does not establish an evolutionary sequence or 零’s earliest graphic form. [ref003, ref025]

The Shuowen explanation gives 令 as the sound element, while the Duan Yucai reading reported in the Taiwan dictionary gives 霝. The available evidence does not explain whether this difference reflects textual transmission or another analysis. [ref012, ref019]

uncertainties.text: No verified oracle-bone or bronze form of 零, or specific early inscription attestation, is established in this dossier. A claim that oracle-bone 零 depicts raindrops is therefore not adopted. [ref004, ref021, ref025, ref026]
The cited Shijing phrase supports an early literary use of 零 with 雨, but its composition date and earliest surviving witness are unresolved. [ref015, ref019]

Dictionaries attest falling, scattered or residual quantities, and zero, but the evidence does not date each transition or establish one complete semantic chain. The reported 1248 placeholder account was not verified; evidence about the separate round sign 〇 does not establish 零’s use as zero. [ref004, ref012, ref019, ref020, ref027]

senses.text: The Shuowen glosses 零 as “remaining rain,” and the Shijing phrase 零雨其濛 supplies a literary use with 雨. The poem’s composition date and earliest surviving witness are not established here, so this is the earliest supported sense in the dossier, not a claim about the word’s original meaning. [ref003, ref012, ref015, ref019]
Later cited uses and commentary attest the sense “fall” and related falling of rain, snow, frost, or dew. Their dates and relation to the rain sense are not established here. [ref012, ref019, ref020]

Dictionary accounts record scattered or residual quantities, fragments, and remainders. The evidence does not date these senses or show a single path by which they developed from “falling rain.” [ref002, ref012, ref019, ref020]

零 is used for the number zero, a current standardized numeric use. Its first attestation as zero is not established here; the reported 1248 placeholder account remains unverified. [ref006, ref016, ref019]

developments.text: The attested falling sense is compatible with an extension from falling rain, but the evidence does not date or document the transition directly. [ref003, ref020]
The senses are attested, but their chronological or semantic connection is not established; no transition is asserted. [ref002, ref012, ref019, ref020]
A source proposes that zero developed from the idea of a small amount remaining, but the consulted evidence does not date or independently verify that transition. [ref004, ref019, ref027]

limitations.text: The dossier supports rain/falling, scattered or residual quantities, and zero as senses, but does not establish a dated sequence connecting all of them. [ref012, ref019, ref020]
The Shijing example is not assigned a precise date here, and no verified first use of 零 for zero is supplied. [ref015, ref027]

overview.text: 零 combines 雨 for rain with 令 as the traditional sound element. It is used for falling rain and for zero, though the evidence here does not date how the later meaning arose. [ref003, ref012, ref016]

components.text: 雨 points to the rain meaning. [ref003, ref012]
令 is traditionally analyzed as the sound element; the exact intended historical reading remains uncertain. [ref003, ref014, ref022]

relationships.text: In the received sound-and-meaning analysis of 零, 雨 contributes the rain category. [ref003, ref012]

Shuowen tradition identifies 令 as the sound element. One 令 reading and 零 share the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction *[r]ˤiŋ and Middle Chinese notation leng, but 令 has multiple readings and this comparison does not uniquely establish which was intended. [ref003, ref014, ref022]
